# Brand Voice

Curated by Skill Harbor: a voice-capture skill that builds a durable, reusable writing-style profile from your real source material instead of defaulting to generic AI copy. The workflow gathers 5 to 20 representative samples (recent X posts first, then articles, essays, launch notes, newsletters, real outbound emails that worked, product docs and site copy), extracts rhythm, sentence length, capitalization norms, parenthetical use, claim sharpness, and what the author never does, then outputs a structured VOICE PROFILE block that downstream skills consume directly. It has strong opinions, encoded as hard bans: fake curiosity hooks, "not X, just Y", "no fluff", forced lowercase, LinkedIn thought-leader cadence, bait questions, and "Excited to share" all get deleted and rewritten. This is the canonical voice layer of the ECC family: content-engine, crosspost, email-ops, investor-outreach, and lead-intelligence (several also in this batch) are all designed to consume its VOICE PROFILE rather than re-deriving style. By @affaan-m, listed here with credit to its creator. From the affaan-m/ECC repository (MIT). Honest caveats: the profile is only as good as your samples, thin source material gives thin voice; it deliberately refuses to store personal voice fingerprints in repo-tracked files unless you ask. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use.
